name: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Radius

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Radius

criteria.description: Presence of a nonunion or pseudoarthrosis of the radius identified at birth or early infancy
Radiographic evidence of segmental bone defect or pseudoarthrosis in the radius with sclerosis and bone deformity
No history of trauma or fracture preceding the pseudoarthrosis
Presence of soft tissue contractures or deformities around the affected forearm

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital onset with radiographic evidence of radial pseudoarthrosis without preceding trauma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be considered to rule out associated syndromes.

searchTerms: birth defect causing radial bone nonunion
radial bone false joint present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Forearm deformity with angulation at the pseudoarthrosis site
searchTerms: forearm bone bending at false joint
difficulty turning palm up or down

common.symptomName: Soft tissue contracture around the affected radius
Mild localized swelling at the pseudoarthrosis site

occasional.notes: May present as paresthesia or numbness in the radial nerve distribution
searchTerms: nerve pain or numbness in forearm
tingling or weakness from radial nerve

occasional.symptomName: Mild pain localized to the forearm
Skin dimpling or scarring over the pseudoarthrosis site
searchTerms: skin dimples or scars over bone
skin changes at false joint site
nerve and blood vessel problems in forearm
circulation and nerve compromise in arm

rare.notes: May include café-au-lait spots and neurofibromas
searchTerms: skin and nerve signs of NF1

imaging: X-ray showing segmental bone defect and sclerosis at the radius with pseudoarthrosis formation
MRI may show soft tissue contractures and exclude other pathologies
genetic: Possible association with NF1 gene mutations in some cases
No specific gene mutation identified as causative for isolated congenital pseudoarthrosis of the radius
other: Clinical examination revealing forearm deformity and limited range of motion

distinguishingFeatures: Different anatomical location and clinical presentation
History of trauma or fracture preceding nonunion
Radiographic features consistent with fracture healing complications

redFlags: Neurovascular compromise signs such as numbness or weakness
Presence of multiple café-au-lait spots suggesting neurofibromatosis
references: Orphanet: Congenital pseudoarthrosis of the radius - ORPHA:295024

Deng X, et al. Clinical features and management of congenital pseudoarthrosis of the radius. Orthop Surg. 2020.
